title: Jade Legacy
author: Lee, Fonda
review:
There's a lot packed into this book, and the sheer ambition, character work, and plot is enough to make this a five star read. I wouldn't say this is one of my all time favorite reads, or even up there with the best I've read this year, but I did enjoy my time with it. This one reads as a number of story vignettes that utilize the characters we're familiar with through a large chunk of time that has some characters grow old, some grow up, and some die, horribly and tragically.

One of my critiques is that it doesn't feel like a cohesive narrative as much, that while it's very interesting and engaging, what it's building towards thematically doesn't connect with me as much as some of my favorite books. While I admire the ambition here, what the author is trying to comment on and build outside of the plot isn't done as well as some of my other favorite authors might do. That being said, the plot and characters are all really well done and it's fun to read having no idea what can happen next is compelling.

We’re both getting old, and our enemies are still young.”

“I was angry at you for a long time after you refused to wear jade. Of course you remember. Now, though… I’m thankful you’re not a Fist, Andy. I need—” Hilo’s voice faltered. “I need one of my brothers to live.”
You’d think it would be easier to face death as you get older, but it doesn’t work that way. You get more attached to life, to people you love and things that are worth living for.”

Jade had meaning because of the type of person one had to become to wear it. Jade was the visible proof that a person had dedicated their life to the discipline of wielding power, to the dangers and costs of being a Green Bone.

The thing about brilliant, elegant plans is that it doesn’t take much to fuck them up.”
